title: Bug: Check intermittently red on dev - a git child in a code-map run is killed (signal SIGTERM) and reported as an error
description:
NOT STARTED. Check fails intermittently on dev itself and on PRs, on the Linux runner; Docs, Package and Tracker integrity stay green. Signature: GlyphError 'git -c did not report an exit status (signal SIGTERM)' thrown from guarded() at src/codemap.ts:441 via buildCodeMap (codemap.ts:552) and produceCodeMap (codemap.ts:397), called from test/parity.test.ts:162. A second signature, test/stream.test.ts (a cold CLI subprocess took 5.1 s and bun's 5 s default killed it, code-map exit code null), is addressed by glyph-cli#102 (bunfig.toml test timeout 60 s plus setDefaultTimeout in test/stream.test.ts), which does NOT fix the parity signature.
Evidence (run ids and Check job ids): run 45100876753 job 137451193804 (dev after #99, codemap.ts:441); run 45101234884 job 137452308091 (dev after #100, test/stream.test.ts:266); run 45101379493 jobs 137452769988 and 137453705490 (#101, stream test, code-map exit null); run 45101738310 job 137453907838 (#102 head 5f488ba, parity, SIGTERM); run 45102143367 job 137455186669 (#102 head a302282 with the 60 s timeout, parity again). Loaded-runner timing: Check took 2m20 to 3m on the failing runs against about 1m05 on earlier green ones, and several PR runs overlapped.
HYPOTHESIS, NOT SHOWN: spawnLimits (src/git.ts) caps a git read's timeout at the remaining wall-time budget with Math.max(1, ceil(left)). When the child is killed at that cap, proc.timedOut is false and proc.signal is SIGTERM; stopIfBudgetSpent(budgeted) then throws BudgetExpired only if activeBudget.expired() has already flipped. A kill at the deadline's rounding edge leaves expired() false and the read becomes an indeterminate error instead of a stop. What is NOT shown: that the budget is the cause (the parity run might use no budget at all), that the pre-GCLI-46 Bun.spawnSync path behaved differently, or that load alone explains it. Reproduce before fixing.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the failure is reproduced locally, for example by running test/parity.test.ts repeatedly under CPU load, and the reproduction (command, load, failure rate, the error text) is recorded in the task notes (proof: the recorded command and its failing output)

the root cause is identified from the reproduction and recorded, stating whether the code-map time budget, a git timeout, or something else sent the SIGTERM (proof: a note naming the cause with the evidence that distinguishes it from the other two)

only after the cause is recorded: a fix in src/codemap.ts and src/git.ts, with a test that forces a tiny budget and proves a stop (truncated, not an error) (proof: the test fails without the fix and passes with it)
a mutation proof that the new test goes red when the fix is removed (proof: recorded mutation run naming the failing test)
the fix landed with an Opus review at the exact head (proof: review verdict recorded in the task notes)

implementationNotes: 2026-11-23 reproduction attempt (worker, local macOS, bun 1.3.14, 10 cores; script: N busy 'while :; do :; done' loops, then bun test test/parity.test.ts repeated). NOT YET REPRODUCED: the SIGTERM signature ('git -c did not report an exit status (signal SIGTERM)') did not occur in any run. Measured: (a) default 5 s bun test timeout, 30 loops: 5/5 runs fail, each at 'hostile global config gives the same bytes' with 'this test timed out after 5000ms' (7.9-9.0 s) - the #102 signature, not SIGTERM. (b) bun test --timeout 60000: 30 loops 5/5 green; 150 loops, bun 1.3.14, 10 runs: 2 red, both a DIFFERENT fault: byte mismatch against the golden with EMPTY omissions (a pointer's lineRanges [] where the golden has ['line 1'], once on file-cap, once on special-paths; confirmed by a temporary console.error of output.omissions, reverted) - so under load the code map can return a wrong, non-truncated output with no time-budget row; unexplained, needs its own root cause. 150 loops, bun 1.4.4 (homebrew; CI pins 1.4.2): 6/6 green. EVIDENCE AGAINST THE HYPOTHESIS: spawnSync's own timeout sets error.code ETIMEDOUT on bun 1.3.14, bun 1.4.4 and node, so a kill at the budget cap reaches git() in src/codemap.ts with proc.timedOut TRUE and the message would read '(timeout)'. The failing CI text reads '(signal SIGTERM)', i.e. timedOut false: the SIGTERM did not come from spawnSync's timeout. The only other documented source in src/spawn.ts is a maxBuffer overflow (ENOBUFS; GIT_MAX_BUFFER is 32 MiB in codemap.ts, implausible for the fixtures) - otherwise an external SIGTERM to the child. So the budget-rounding hypothesis is contradicted by the error text itself; the sender is still unidentified. Next: find what could SIGTERM a git child on the CI runner, reproduce with the CI-pinned bun 1.4.2 (not installed locally; an unpinned npx download was refused by the permission layer and was not retried).

FINDING B (separate from the SIGTERM signature; measured 2026-11-23, local, bun 1.3.14, 150 busy loops, test/parity.test.ts with --timeout 60000, temporary console.error instrumentation in grepLines reverted): the wrong-output fault is a git grep that exits 0 with EMPTY stdout and EMPTY stderr. In grepLines (src/codemap.ts:306) status 0 with no stdout parses to no ranges, so the pointer is returned with lineRanges [] and rangesRead true: no time-budget row, no omission, reason unchanged, i.e. a silently wrong result. Seen as 'REPRO-GREP0-EMPTY' + 'REPRO-GREP0-NOLINES' (status 0, stdout '', stderr ''): 7 failing runs of 40 across the instrumented batches, on identifiers alphaWidget, ledgerTotals, longPathMarkerA/B. Re-running the IDENTICAL git grep immediately afterwards (same spawn path) returned status 0 with the full stdout (478 and 90 bytes) in all 4 retried cases, so the fault is transient. Not reproduced in isolation: 3 x 3000 spawnSync('echo hello') under the same load on bun 1.3.14, bun 1.4.4 and node, 0 empty stdout, 0 non-zero. So it is NOT yet attributed: it is either bun's spawnSync dropping stdout of a successful child, or git itself, and only git-specific probing can say; the retry shows the output exists and is deterministic when read again. Consequence: any git read in src/codemap.ts can silently return empty on a loaded host, so a successful empty read cannot be told from a lost one; GCLI-51's fix scope must cover this fault in addition to (or instead of) the SIGTERM one.

CORRECTION to FINDING B counts: across the four 10-run batches (40 runs) the empty-stdout event was logged 9 times (1, 4, 0 and 4 per batch; one earlier uninstrumented batch is not counted), and 8 of 40 runs ended red; not every red run carried a logged event, and some reds in the hostile-config test were not attributed. The '7 of 40' above is wrong. Only 4 events had the immediate retry logged; all 4 retried clean.
